entry.label: Magnus Ramage
entry.description: An Open University systems scholar and educator whose work connects the history of systems thinking, sociotechnical information systems, critical and decolonial approaches, and the construction of systems canons.
entry.canonical_definition: An Open University systems scholar and educator whose work connects the history of systems thinking, sociotechnical information systems, critical and decolonial approaches, and the construction of systems canons.

profile.summary: Ramage connects systems history, sociotechnical information systems, critical inquiry and the active problem of who is allowed to count as a systems thinker.
profile.canonical_definition: Ramage connects systems history, sociotechnical information systems, critical inquiry and the active problem of who is allowed to count as a systems thinker.
profile.why_it_matters: His work makes canon construction part of systems practice rather than treating a list of recognised figures as neutral inheritance.
key_distinctions: biographical history versus a final canon
critical and decolonial inquiry versus adding decorative diversity
common_misreadings: Treating Systems Thinkers as an objective ranking misses the authors' own boundary questions.
Treating decolonisation as demographic decoration leaves the knowledge rules unchanged.
open_checks: Add published outputs from the systems-thinking-from-the-margins work when available.
Trace the Open University teaching lineage in more detail.
profile.context_and_lineage: Institutional and intellectual context: The Open University; systems history; sociotechnical information systems; critical and decolonial approaches. No ethnicity is inferred or assigned.
